chunks: My father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with them) both said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abu Nasr al-Bazanti, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him, 'Some of our companions say determinism (jabr), and some say ability (istita'ah).' He said to me, 'Write down:'

Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, said: 'O son of Adam! By My Will you were, you are the one who wills for yourself whatever you will, and by My Power you fulfilled My obligations, and by My Bounty you were strengthened to disobey Me. I made you hearing, seeing, and strong. Whatever good reaches you is from Allah, and whatever evil reaches you is from your own self. And this is that I am worthier of your good deeds than yourself, and you are worthier of your bad deeds than I am. And this is that I will not be asked about what I do, while they will be asked. I have arranged for you everything you wish.'

key_terms.مِنْ نَفْسِكَ: From your self (attributing evil to human agency)

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia view on Jabr (determinism) and Istita'ah (ability) according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) elucidates the Shia doctrine of *al-Amr bayn al-Amrayn* (the matter between the two matters), reconciling divine omnipotence with human agency by asserting that while all capacity and will are granted by God, the moral responsibility for choices rests with the individual. This narration highlights that God is more deserving of credit for human good deeds due to His prior bestowal of ability, whereas humans bear the primary burden for their sins, a nuance that distinguishes Shia theology from strict predestination or pure free will.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 6. My father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with them) both said: Sa`d ibn `Abd Allah said, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn `Isa, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abu Nasr al-Bazanfi that Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (AS) said:
I asked him, “Some of our scholars believe in determinism [jabr], while others believe in ability [istita`ah].” Therefore, he (AS) replied to me, Write down:

Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, said: O son of Adam! Your will is subject to My Will. You fulfill your obligations through My Power, and through My Bounty you have the strength to disobey me. I have made you seeing, hearing, and strong. Whatever good reaches you is from Allah, and whatever evil reaches you is from your own self. So I am worthier of your goods deeds than yourself, and you are worthier of your bad deeds than I am. This is why I will not be asked about what I do, while you will be asked about what you did. I have made systematic for you everything you wish.
